_meta.what: Independent ground-truth labels for the 7 distinct llm-eligible experimental cases, established by reading real disclosed source. SEPARATE from scanner state: scanner_emitted_bucket is what TChecker produced; verified_* is human analysis of the real program and MUST be independently reviewed before any accuracy claim.
_meta.authoring: Hand-verified against the cached vulnerable/patched source (Claude analysis). NOT machine-derived. Treat as a reviewable claim, not settled truth.
_meta.differential_note: case_identity.py flags a vuln!=patched differential by function-body TEXT. For the mozjpeg cases the fix is in the BUFSIZE macro the identical body references, so the effective capacity differs though the text does not -- marked effective_capacity_differential here.
_meta.boundary: No experimental condition (A/B/C) was consulted in establishing these labels. Condition B was NOT run first.

cases.evidence: block = PORT_Alloc(modulusLen); bp = block; a series of *bp++ writes fill padLen padding bytes. VULN declares `int padLen`; the disclosed fix (this exact function) changes it to `unsigned int padLen` and tightens the length handling so the pad/data cannot exceed modulusLen. This is the disclosed CVE-2019-17006 site.
cases.evidence_relative_answer: With only local facts the write-vs-capacity relation is genuinely unresolved (bp bound depends on padLen/data->len vs modulusLen). Ground truth differs by revision; the scanner is correctly uncertain in BOTH.

cases.evidence: JOCTET _buffer[BUFSIZE] is a local array written through a cursor by the Huffman coder. VULN BUFSIZE=(DCTSIZE2*2)+8=136; the disclosed fix (Debian #768369) doubles it to (DCTSIZE2*4)=256. The function source text is identical across revisions; only the referenced macro (hence the array's real capacity) changes.
cases.evidence_relative_answer: The count-vs-capacity relation is unresolved without evaluating BUFSIZE. Vulnerable in the 136-byte build, safe in the 256-byte build.

cases.evidence: Same _buffer[BUFSIZE] mechanism as encode_one_block, in the same file, fixed by the same BUFSIZE change. NOT an independent bug from encode_one_block -- same CVE, same buffer, same fix.
cases.evidence_relative_answer: Same as encode_one_block; counts as the SAME underlying defect, not a second independent vulnerable case.

cases.cve: incidental (in CVE-2019-11745/11759 file, unchanged by both)
cases.evidence: buffer_len = SharedSecret->len + 4 + SharedInfoLen; buffer = PORT_Alloc(buffer_len). The destination is allocated locally to exactly fit what is written into it, guarded by `key_len > 254*HashLen` rejection. Writes are bounded by buffer_len.
cases.evidence_relative_answer: Locally provable-safe by construction (alloc sized to content); the scanner abstains only because it does not relate the symbolic buffer_len alloc to the write extent. Same in both revisions (incidental candidate).

cases.evidence: buf is an out-parameter (void *buf); the PBE key bytes are copied into it. The capacity of buf is the CALLER's responsibility and is not visible in this function. Safe-or-not depends on caller-provided sizing not traced here.
cases.evidence_relative_answer: Genuinely unresolved without interprocedural caller evidence -- matches the scanner's capacity_relation_not_established. Unchanged across the CVE revisions.

cases.evidence: Same function as nsc_pbe_key_gen/buf@11745 but a slightly different revision of the body (46 vs 40 lines); same out-parameter structure. NEARLY the same case -- weakly independent.
cases.evidence_relative_answer: Same reasoning as the 11745 copy. Should NOT be counted as a fully independent case from it.

cases.cve: incidental (CVE-2016-1950 file, unchanged at this site)
cases.evidence: copy = sec_asn1d_alloc(pool, len); PORT_Memcpy(copy, data, len). sec_asn1d_alloc returns a block of exactly `len` usable bytes (it is a thin arena wrapper), so the memcpy of `len` bytes is in bounds. Establishing that requires reading the allocator's contract -- exactly what the scanner routed to contract review.
cases.evidence_relative_answer: Safe once the sec_asn1d_alloc contract (returns >= len) is established -- a contract-review task, correctly routed. Unchanged across revisions.
